questions.question: When N is divided by 10 the remainder is 8. What is the remainder when N is divided by 5.
questions.solution:
We can write, N = 10k + 8

⇒ N/5 = (10k + 8)/5 = 2k + 8/5

∴ Remainder = 3

⇒ 70, 105 and 140 lies in between 50 and 150, which are divisible by both 5 and 7.

questions.question: What is the unit’s digit of 237 × 432 × 156?
questions.solution:
Concept used:

For finding the unit digit we need not multiply all the numbers, only multiply unit digit

Calculation:

On multiplying units digit of each number, 7 ⨯ 2 ⨯ 6 = 84

∴ we get unit digit as 4.

questions.question: For what value of M, 243M is divisible by 4?
questions.solution:
A number is divisible by 4, if the last two digit of the number is divisible by 4.

Given number = 243M

∴ Last two digit is divisible by 4, only when M = 2 or 6

questions.question: B and C can do a work in 12 days. C and D can do the same work in 18 days. D and B can do the same work in 24 days. In how many days can B, C and D together complete the work?
questions.solution:
Let B , C and D can do the work in b, c and d days respectively.

Given that,

⇒ 1/b + 1/c = 1/12 ----1

⇒ 1/c + 1/d = 1/24 ----2

⇒ 1/b + 1/d = 1/24 ----3

Now adding above three equations, we get,

⇒ 2(1/b + 1/c + 1/d) = 1/12 + 1/18 + 1/24 = (6 + 4 + 3)/72 = 13/72

⇒ (1/b + 1/c + 1/d) = 13/144

∴ B, C and D together can complete the work in 144/13 days.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 30 minutes. Pipe B can fill the same tank in 50 minutes. In how much time (in minutes) both pipes together can fill the same tank?
questions.solution:
LCM of 30 and 50 = 150

Pipe A can fill 5 units of water in 1 min.

Pipe B can fill 3 units of water in 1 min.

Both the pipes can fill 8 units of water in 1 min.

∴ Pipe A and B together can fill 150 units of water in 150/8 = 18.75 min

questions.question: After giving a discount of 20% there is a profit of 20%. If 5% discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let SP = Rs. 100

⇒ MP = Rs. 120

And CP = Rs. 80

If discount given = 5%

⇒ Then SP = 120 – 5% of 120 = Rs. 114

⇒New profit = 114 – 80 = Rs. 34

∴ New profit% = 34 × 100/80 = 42.5%

questions.question: Average of 40 results is 20. Average of 60 results is 30. What is the average of all the results?
questions.solution:
⇒ sum of 40 results = 40 × 20 = 800

⇒ sum of 60 results = 60 × 30 = 1800

Total sum = 2600 and number of results = 100

∴ Average = 2600/100 = 26

questions.question: If the loss percent on an article is 30%, then what is the ratio of the cost price and selling price?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Loss % = 30%

**FORMULA USED:**

Loss % = loss / CP ⨯ 100 

**CALCULATION:**

Loss% = loss/Cp ⨯ 100 = 30

⇒ (Cp – Sp)/Cp = 3/10

⇒ 10 ⨯ CP – 10 ⨯ SP = 3 ⨯ CP

⇒ 7 ⨯ CP = 10 ⨯ SP

∴ CP/SP = 10/7

questions.question: If cost price of an article is 50% of its selling price, then what is the profit percent?
questions.solution:
Let the SP be x.

CP = 0.5x

Profit = 0.5x

∴ Profit% = 0.5x/0.5x × 100 = 100%

questions.question: If A’s salary is 80% of B’s salary, then B’s salary is what percentage of A’s salary?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of A : B = 80 : 100 = 4 : 5

B as a percentage of A = (B / A) × 100

Required percentage = (5 / 4) × 100 = 125%

**∴ The correct answer is 125%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A’s salary = 80% of B’s salary

**Formula Used:**

Percentage = (Value / Base Value) × 100

 
 B's Salary (100 units)
 
 A's Salary (80 units)
 
• 
 B/A × 100 = (100/80) × 100 = 125%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let B’s salary = ₹100

⇒ A’s salary = 80% of 100 = ₹80

⇒ Required Percentage = (B’s Salary / A’s Salary) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (100 / 80) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (5 / 4) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 125%

**∴ The correct answer is 125%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage to a fraction, divide by 100. Example: 80% = 80/100 = 4/5. 125% = 125/100 = 5/4.

Reciprocal Percentages

If A is x% of B, then B is (100 × 100 / x)% of A. Here, 10000 / 80 = 125%.

Percentage Change

Percentage Increase/Decrease = (Difference / Original Value) × 100. Useful when comparing salary hikes or reductions.

questions.question: To qualify an examination of 200 marks, a candidate should obtain 40% marks. If A scores 10% more than the passing marks, then what is the marks obtained by A?
questions.solution:
⇒ Passing marks = 40% of 200 = 80

∴ A’s score = 80 + 10% of 80 = 80 + 8 = 88

questions.question: A train is travelling at the speed of 90 km/hr. How many seconds will it take to cover a distance of 2 km?
questions.solution:
Time = distance/speed

∴ Time taken to cover 2 km = 2/90 ⨯ 60 ⨯ 60 = 80 seconds

questions.question: A train of length 200 m is running at the speed of 60 km/hr. What is the time (in seconds) taken by the train to pass a man standing at the station?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Length of the train = 200m

Speed of the train = 60km/hr

**FORMULA USED:**

Time = Distance/Speed

**CALCULATION:**

∴ Time taken to pass a man standing at the station = 200/(60 ⨯ 5/18) = (200 ⨯ 18)/300 = 12 sec
